Use case: style-transfer / scale correction.
Production opaque portrait scrolling game-map texture, 1024x1536. The supplied city image is the approved STYLE, architecture identity, palette and lighting reference. Retain its pale softly textured roofs, cool blue-grey walls, quiet matte asphalt, restrained trees and local ruin corners. Warm light from upper RIGHT, shadows toward lower LEFT.

PRIMARY CORRECTION: the supplied picture is a CLOSE-UP of one street with huge buildings, making a flying aircraft feel almost roof-height. Redraw it as a MUCH WIDER, HIGHER AERIAL VIEW over SEVERAL CITY BLOCKS. Show approximately 1.8–2 times as much ground in both dimensions. Individual buildings, streets, paving joints, trees and rooftop equipment should be around 50–60% of their former screen size. Do not merely add blur, shrink an aircraft, or move a cloud. Change the GROUND SCENE'S SCALE AND FRAMING.

Compose about 12–16 varied smaller buildings across three lateral groups and several staggered rows, with intersecting side streets, small courtyards, vacant parcels and service lanes. Keep a recognizable loosely central main street, but it occupies roughly 20–25% of width rather than a canyon framed by two enormous roofs. Some secondary streets and neighboring blocks must be visible. The viewer should see a neighborhood below, not a few facades beside them. Keep a broad low-contrast field for airborne combat even over roofs/streets; avoid dense high-contrast clutter.

Paint from a HIGH NEAR-OVERHEAD orthographic bird's-eye camera. Roofs strongly dominate; small narrow shaded side-face strips, a little window/door indication and grounded contact shadows still show height. Short side-wall bands should be around one tenth of projected roof depth. Do not become a flat roof-only blueprint, but do not show long multi-storey fronts. Scale shadows DOWN with the buildings, no huge dark wedges spanning half the screen. Perspective, light, all street grounds and every building must be coherent.

Residential/mixed district identity: smaller L-shaped courtyard blocks, a few stepped roof masses, narrow retail/utility buildings and separated planted courtyards, with varied setbacks and shapes. Avoid cloned square office roofs and repeated paired fans. Keep the same approved rendering finish and restrained local broken corners. Reduce tiny construction/roof/pavement detail appropriately for the longer viewing distance; preserve architectural silhouette and large value planes. Slight cool aerial distance softness in painted values, not a blanket blur filter or strong fog.

MATTE ASPHALT only, subdued non-directional value variation, restrained road marks and sparse repairs. No water ripples, wavy brush ribbons, swirls, gloss, new heavy grunge or oversaturated vegetation. Streets, courtyards and buildings form continuous connected ground, no floating platforms or sticker cutouts. A few small grounded rubble fragments are appropriate but should scale with this higher aerial view.

Scrolling: top and bottom 8–10% are low quiet connecting streets/open paved ground, no tall sliced roof/wall or long severed shadow. Match a centered main street connection, muted asphalt endpoints, and companion texture value/scale. No clouds, fog overlay, aircraft, actors, enemies, bullets, pickups, UI, text, logos, watermark, transparency or extra panels. ONE finished map.

Use case: style-transfer / scale correction. Opaque portrait game-map texture, 1024x1536, ONE finished commercial/office district.
Image 1 is the corrected HIGH AERIAL district: match its smaller ground/building scale, near-overhead projection, pale/cool palette, upper-right light, shadow scale and quiet rendering finish. Image 2 is the previous commercial segment as architecture/material identity reference only; it is MUCH TOO CLOSE and its giant roofs/facades must not be preserved at that size.
Show a wider neighborhood, about 1.8–2 times the former visible ground span in both dimensions. Around 12–16 smaller varied building volumes across three lateral groups and several rows, connected by side streets, delivery courts, paved gaps and small plazas. Individual buildings, trees, curbs, roof details and road marks should be roughly half to three-fifths the old image's displayed size. A loosely central main street is around 20–25% of image width, with neighboring city blocks also visible. Avoid a canyon of two giant buildings.
Commercial identity: several irregular shop strips with restrained muted red awnings, a stepped T-shaped office, small separate retail pavilions, a low entrance glass canopy and delivery courtyards. Different footprints/setbacks, no cloned square roof boxes or repeated twin-fan arrangements. Local moderate corner damage and small grounded debris at corresponding contacts, not wholesale destruction or a road obstacle course.
Vary the urban topology: stagger side-street junctions, share paved lots between some buildings, let a plaza or delivery court span a wider parcel, and give the main street a mild angular offset. Do not put every building in its own identical rounded-rectangle sidewalk island or repeat five perfectly aligned cross-streets.
HIGH NEAR-OVERHEAD orthographic painting. Roofs strongly dominate, retain only narrow foreshortened wall/window/door strips, around one tenth of roof projected depth. A few side faces and short contact shadows show height; no roof-only blueprint and no full multi-storey fronts. All streets, walls, shadows and yards share one ground/projection. Small coherent lower-left shadows from upper-RIGHT sunlight, no huge dark wedges. Preserve the approved pale softly textured concrete/blue-grey glass-wall style; simplify detail for distance and use mild cool atmospheric value grouping rather than blur/fog.
Solid quiet MATTE asphalt with sparse marks, patches and little wear; absolutely no water-like waves, directional flowing brush ribbons, glossy reflections or grunge wash. Continuous ground, thin curbs, restrained green trees, no island platforms or pasted stickers. Combat background stays low contrast.
Top/bottom 8–10% low open street connection ground matching image 1's center endpoint, width/color/scale, with no tall sliced structures. No baked clouds, aircraft, people, enemies, projectiles, pickups, UI, lettering, logos, watermark, transparency or extra panels.

Use case: style-transfer / scale correction. Opaque portrait game-map texture, 1024x1536, ONE finished modern service/workshop district.
Image 1 is the corrected HIGH AERIAL district: match its smaller building/ground scale, high near-overhead projection, approved pale/cool finish, upper-right light and reduced shadow size. Image 2 gives this segment's service/workshop identity but is MUCH TOO CLOSE; change its giant-building framing.
View a broader district with roughly 1.8–2 times as much ground span in each dimension, 12–16 smaller building volumes across three lateral groups and multiple staggered rows. Main and secondary service streets, loading courts, paved yards, utility parcels and planted setbacks are visible together. Buildings, lanes, trees, curbs, equipment and debris all around 50–60% of their previous screen size. A loosely centered main route occupies about 20–25% width, not a canyon between two huge workshop fronts.
Vary ordinary modern service architecture: a few long low workshop roof bays/skylights, smaller brick utility annexes, asymmetrical U-shaped maintenance yard, storage sheds and flat or shallow industrial roofs at different setbacks. Keep restrained local corner damage and correspondingly small ground rubble. No cloned giant office boxes, heavy ruin carpet or gratuitous big props.
Use irregular industrial block spacing and staggered T-junctions: a shared loading court connects several small buildings, one long narrow workshop occupies an offset parcel and a utility yard opens between blocks. Avoid a repetitive grid of identical rounded-rectangle lots or perfectly aligned cross-streets. Keep all buildings genuinely at the smaller aerial scale.
High NEAR-OVERHEAD orthographic painting; roofs strongly dominate, short shaded side/window/door strips about one tenth of projected roof depth remain visible. Preserve enough side face to show volume without tall facades or pure roof-only schematic. All architecture, paving, ground contacts and moderate lower-left shadows share coherent upper-RIGHT light. Reduce shadow reach and fine material detail to suit this farther viewpoint. Match existing soft pale concrete, blue-grey walls/glass, muted slate asphalt and controlled green trees, with mild cool aerial value grouping, not whole-image blur.
SOLID MATTE asphalt, sparse wear/repairs/marks, no water ripples, wave bands, diagonal flowing strokes, wet shine, noisy grime or floating-platform bevels. Physical continuous street/yard ground, no pasted building stickers. Low contrast for airborne combat.
Top/bottom 8–10% quiet low open street connection matching image 1's centered endpoints, width/value/scale, no severed tall roof/wall/shadow. No clouds/fog overlay, aircraft, actors, enemies, projectiles, pickups, UI, text, logos, watermark, transparency or comparison panels.
